$comment: THE STAGE TABLE — the one place a stage's status is recorded.
`scripts/docs.test.mjs` reads this file. Two rules make it more than a list:
1. A stage may not be `shipped` while any `DEFER(engine-N)` marker in the
tree names it. A stage table that has started lying is worse than none,
because it is re-read and believed by somebody with no memory.
2. Every guard's `stage` names a row here, so a guard cannot protect work
that is not on the map.
`ends` is the exit criterion — an observable, not a feeling. It is what makes
`shipped` a claim somebody could check rather than a decision somebody made.

stages.title: Ground — workspace, docs, guard registry, standards
Kernel — entities, declarations, gate algebra, problems
Directory + placement
Runtime — manifest → live worker
Identity + tenancy
Surface — HeroUI shell, nav, sky, rendered settings
Money — plans, entitlements, credits, jobs
Services — ai and notify over RPC
Vault + legal
A real product on OneEngine, end to end
One — the deployment and the OneSpace
The agent surface — every operation an MCP tool, derived
Multi-app access — a platform role for the workspace, a role per app inside it
The package rail — a priced bundle of timed grants, one ledger, one clock
The tenant centre — the shell with the router: five areas + app screens inside
The operator console — the same shell on `admin.`, and the maintenance switch
AI actions — a lane per action, a model the operator binds, words that narrow
OneSpace — one surface over the product, reachable from every door, addressed
OneDesign — the design system named, packaged, documented and fenced
Workspaces — personal or commercial, one brand, one installable, a shard of their own
Payment — a workspace subscribes, and only a signed event stamps the plan
OneSpace — `id`, `admin` and `setup` merge into one address off the workspace root
Mail that leaves the process — a letter, its variables, and a provider
A workspace composes its own roles out of one app's keys
Agreements — versioned documents, an acceptance per person per version, and the wall until there is one
The vault is opened — consent, who looked, your data, and an erasure that shreds
The AI lane runs — a catalogue that syncs itself, one door out to every provider, a charge built on what the call really cost, and a nightly check against the bill we are sent
Notifications are filed — an event raised becomes a note in somebody's inbox
The daily sweep — erasure happens on a clock, and every run is recorded
A workspace's apps are turned on and off, and a workspace can move shard
Account security — sign out everywhere, and proving it is you again before something irreversible
A manifest changes while the deployment is up, and the composed surface forgets
A guard refuses a declared setting nothing names — the seam a handler reads one through is live; the completeness check over it is not
The kernel's remaining conveniences are each used by a lane or removed
A workspace runs its own retention ladder against its own customers, and ours freezes it
The deployment provisions itself — a product declares what it needs underneath it, and the reconciler makes it exist in the right jurisdiction, binds it, and reaps it after a drain
A workspace's records change shard, which is the only way its jurisdiction can — read-only while it copies, verified before it flips, and the source drained rather than emptied

A notification leaves the process — Web Push written out rather than depended on, a subscription filed under the door it was made at so it wears that workspace's own icon, and a keypair the console generates and never accepts
The documentation is two generated pages — what exists, derived from the engine; and how to add to it, which no generator can derive
An app ships a screen — a product's browser half is a chunk of its own, loaded when its workspace opens it, drawing that workspace's own records through the door it is handed
A workspace's brand reaches the screen — the surfaces it picked, and only the ones its products have
A screen asks the gate before it draws a control, rather than after it is pressed
Hello's remaining screens reach the workspace's own records — the report against its target, and writing a note
A one-off purchase — a credit pack, and becoming a business — through the same checkout
A plan is edited from the console, and everybody already on it keeps what they were sold
The wallet tops itself up — a standing instruction, a cooldown, and a decline the customer can read
Storage is metered rather than refused — the included amount is where the meter starts, and an empty wallet costs the writes and never the files
The deployment's legal identity is complete — the registered address it is written to, and whether selling where it sells needs a representative there
stages.ends: `IDENTITY.address` is the address on the licence rather than the Emirate, and either a representative is declared beside the sub-processors or a written decision says none is needed for where this deployment sells

stages.title: A stranger joins a workspace by themselves — a door the workspace opens, a role the app names, and a ceiling the plan sells (D23)
stages.ends: an app declares `access.joining`, composition refuses a joining role that is not a customer or that reads a tenant-scoped collection, `me.join` resolves its workspace from the door, and the customer ceiling refuses with a sentence naming the upgrade

stages.title: The interface speaks a second language — dictionaries, a language control, and the copy guard reading both
stages.ends: `Presentation.language` is offered on the Formats screen, every written string in `@engine/design` and `engine/one-space` resolves through a dictionary, and `tone.test.mjs` checks the voice in each language rather than only in English

stages.title: A collection says `searchable` and becomes findable — the write marks, a pass carries, erasure removes, and one filter is the boundary
stages.ends: `searchable` on a `CollectionSpec` produces the ledger, the `<collection>.search` operation, the quarter-hourly index pass and the removal on delete and on erasure, with `searching.test.mjs` making each of the four silences a test failure.

stages.title: The words arrive as they are written — one metered run, streamed, and the charge rides the last token
stages.ends: `ctx.stream` answers with an SSE `Response` from the same reserve, model and words `ctx.generate` uses; `generateStream` holds the same four bounds; a cancelled stream settles at the reserve and is corrected by the nightly check; `metering.test.mjs` asks the streaming lane every question it asks the other.

stages.title: A workspace asks to change its jurisdiction, and the ask is the only thing that is new
stages.ends: A workspace with `tenant:manage` can request a residency change from its own settings; the request is recorded and answered by an operator rather than granted, because Cloudflare fixes a database's jurisdiction at creation and the move is `op.tenant.move`'s `into` either way. `operator.test.mjs` sees the read behind the operator's queue of them, and nothing in the request path can begin a move by itself.

stages.title: A collection's `offline` policy reaches the browser — a write survives no signal, and a read answers without one
stages.ends: `offline` is read by the runtime and by the browser rather than only declared: `queue` holds a write until there is a connection and replays it once, `cache` answers a read from what was last seen and says how old it is, and `none` is honest about failing. `scripts/declared.test.mjs` fails on any field of a kernel declaration that no lane reads, which is the check that would have found this one.

stages.title: A collection narrows to part of a workspace — a location grant, and one filter the platform composes
stages.ends: `within: { column, tree }` on a `CollectionSpec` makes the generated verbs answer only what the caller's location grants reach, composed in the one function that owns the boundary exactly as `subject` scope is; no grants means the whole workspace; a notification's audience narrows the same way; and a guard refuses a handler composing that filter itself.

stages.title: A family takes a hue — one declared per product, never written at a call site
stages.ends: `tint` carries more than one hue, each declared once in `scene/tint.ts` as a constraint on the family, chosen by name rather than by value; `scene.test.mjs` still refuses a colour written into a screen; and two products wearing the family are visibly different and neither is nameable.

stages.title: Records move between workspaces — a garage becomes a business and its history goes with it
stages.ends: A workspace's records can be handed to another workspace the same account can already reach, with the ledger's provenance carried rather than restamped, refused where the destination's apps do not cover the source's collections, and audited on both sides. Until it exists the only path is an export and an import, which loses who did what and when.

stages.title: An operation's ceiling is in force — calls per minute, per caller, refused rather than declared
stages.ends: `OperationSpec.rate` is read inside `performOperation`, so both doors obey it and neither can forget; a caller past the ceiling is refused with a catalogued problem naming when to try again; and the counter is bounded rather than a row per call.

stages.title: A write says it worked — the sentence the operation declared, and the reads it made stale
stages.ends: `OperationSpec.outcome` reaches the browser and is applied by the one door: a successful write raises its declared message in its declared tone exactly once, and every operation it names in `invalidates` is re-read rather than left showing what was true before the press.
